prompt: Find members by id in an id-sorted roster with Collections.binarySearch and a Comparator.comparingInt key comparator, returning -1 for a miss and decoding the insertion point from the negative result.
explanation: Collections.binarySearch's three-argument form compares with a Comparator instead of Comparable, which lets a record with no natural ordering be searched by any single field. The search still needs something to compare the elements against, so you hand it a throwaway probe object whose only meaningful field is the one the comparator reads. On a miss the method returns -(insertion point) - 1, a scheme that keeps every miss negative and distinguishable from index 0; -hit - 1 inverts it.
hints: Comparator.comparingInt(RosterMember::id) is the comparator; pass it as the third argument to Collections.binarySearch.
Build a probe with new RosterMember(id, "") -- the name is never looked at by that comparator.
A negative result r encodes the insertion point as -r - 1; a non-negative result is already the index.
